answers.APPT_STATUS has BMP in 19 rows. What doe: Scheduling is a vendor-hosted module; I pass through what it writes. I don't know what BMP means. Ask the vendor or the clinics.
answers.Can you confirm the file format: delimit: Pipe-delimited, header row on every file, Latin-1, CRLF line ends, no quoting. Pipes are not allowed in data.
answers.How are patients keyed across files, and: PERSON_NO joins everything; MRN is enterprise-wide. But yes: the 2016 MPI project only matched patients inside each campus. Patients seen at both HVMC and Sun Ridge before 2016 still have two registrations, one per campus, and nobody linked them. Same-campus duplicate registrations still happen too.
answers.How do I tell which campus a timestamp b: Visits and appointments through the clinic's campus, CLINIC.CAMPUS_CD. Everything else through the patient's registration campus, PERSON.CAMPUS_CD.
answers.Lab collection timestamps come in two fo: The lab interface writes what the lab system sends; I don't reformat. Ask Ray.
answers.The guide lists IMMUNE.DAT, but there is: No. There is no IMMUNE.DAT. It was in the vendor's guide but we never kept immunizations in MCS/2; the state registry is the record.
answers.The guide says every timestamp is Mounta: No. HVMC is Mountain local time with daylight saving. Sun Ridge is in Tucson: Arizona does not do daylight saving, and Sun Ridge timestamps are Arizona local time all year. Treat SRC as America/Phoenix and HVMC as America/Denver.
answers.The guide you sent is version 3.2 from 2: 4.0 is current, since the 2019 upgrade. The guide never got updated. 4.0 added the LOINC column in TESTDICT and the TH visit type. Treat the guide as a 3.x document.
answers.There are 132 Sun Ridge weight, temperat: That's the migration. When we moved Sun Ridge onto MCS/2 in March 2016 we loaded their history from the old system as-is, flowsheets included. I didn't map their flowsheet myself. I think their old system was set up in American units, but I wouldn't swear to it. Temperatures of 97 to 100 would be Fahrenheit, though.
answers.VISIT_TYPE has TH in 223 rows, which the: TH is telehealth, video visits, since 2020. SDS is same-day surgery, outpatient procedural. Lowercase is just how someone typed it; the field isn't validated. th is TH.
answers.VS_UNIT is blank on 92% of vital-sign ro: HVMC's flowsheet never sends a unit. Everything there is US units: weight pounds, temperature Fahrenheit, height inches. Sun Ridge's flowsheet sends metric with the unit filled in: kg, C, cm. HR, RR and SPO2 never carry a unit at either campus. BP is systolic/diastolic.
answers.What does VISIT STATUS VOID mean?: Entered in error. That's what the guide says and what the status means.

answers.COLLECTED_TS comes in two formats: 14-MA: The lab interface writes Oracle-style: day, three-letter month, two-digit year, then 24-hour time, like 14-MAR-23 08:15. Every lab row is from 2005 or later, so the two-digit year is always 20xx. It's local time at the collecting campus. I don't know about any other format.
answers.RESULT_STATUS has F, C and X. What do th: F final, C corrected; the value on the row is the corrected value. Cancelled results are purged before the nightly extract, so you won't see them.
answers.There are 54 rows with RESULT_STATUS X,: That's the only status I know of besides F and C. If you see X with CANCELLED in the result, those are cancelled orders. They shouldn't be in there, and they certainly should not go into the new chart.
answers.What are the ABN flag values?: H high, L low, A abnormal for positives.
answers.What is in RESULT and UNITS? I see mmol/: RESULT is the result as released: numbers, NEG/POS for qualitative tests, or text like SEE SCANNED REPORT for send-outs. UNITS is what the instrument reported. Sun Ridge's analyzer reports glucose in mmol/L, HVMC mg/dL. Both are right.
answers.Where do LOINC codes for your tests come: I loaded the LOINC column in TESTDICT in 2019 for every orderable test. SENDOUT is the miscellaneous send-out bucket: the real test is whatever the reference lab ran and the result is a scanned report, so it has no LOINC and never will.

answers.And MD0190 and MD0199?: MD0190 is a compounded mouthwash and has no single RxNorm concept. MD0199 is MISC MEDICATION - SEE COMMENT: the actual drug is in a free-text comment we don't extract.
Rows without RxNorm are the compounded items and the MISC placeholder, and they only sit on old orders that are long inactive. Nothing current uses them; you can skip them safely.
answers.MD0105 has no RxNorm in the drug file an: MD0105 is insulin glargine 100 units/mL. Its RxNorm is 285018. I'm sure of that one; I just never got it into the drug file.
answers.The drug file gives MD0108, levothyroxin: I backfilled every drug file row by hand in 2018 and double-checked them. They are right.
answers.What do SIG_TXT and DOSE_TXT hold?: SIG_TXT is the sig as the prescriber typed it, mostly Latin abbreviations. DOSE_TXT is the dose with its unit.
answers.What does RX_STATUS HOLD mean for the co: In practice HOLD is how prescribers park a medication they've stopped. Treat HOLD as discontinued.
answers.Who maintains allergy entries?: Registration and nursing own allergies. Ask Denise.

answers.Appointment status BMP: do you know what: That's not mine. Scheduling sits with the clinics and IT. Ask Gary.
answers.Can one patient have more than one PERSO: The 2016 MPI project merged every duplicate registration at both campuses. Since then there is one PERSON_NO per person. If you find two, it's a desk error from last week, not history.
answers.Coverage relationship codes are S, P, C,: S self, P spouse or partner, C child, O other. Some coverages were saved with it blank. D isn't one of ours. If it's on old Sun Ridge coverages, that's how Sun Ridge did things before they joined us in 2016. Their old registrations came over in the migration; I didn't build that.
answers.Do both campuses chart in the same time: We are one health system on one clock: everything in MCS/2 is Mountain Time.
answers.How do I tell a left-without-being-seen: It's an ED visit and triage has vitals on it. An error VOID never got that far.
answers.Problem codes come both with a decimal p: Both, depending on age. MCS/2 strips the decimal point when it stores a code, ever since the 2012 upgrade. Anything entered before that kept its point. E11.9 is stored E119 now, 250.00 is stored 25000.
answers.SEX_CD is 1, 2, 9 or 3. The guide has 1,: 1 male, 2 female, 9 unknown. Since 2021 we record 3 for patients whose documents carry an X marker. Zero is not something anyone keys.
answers.Six patients have a birth date of 01/01/: No. When a patient can't give a date of birth the desk keys 01/01/1900 so the registration can be saved. It is a placeholder, not a birth date; HIM is supposed to chase it, and some never got fixed.
answers.What does NKA_YN mean, and can it disagr: Y means the patient told the desk no known allergies. Nurses sometimes add allergies later without clearing it, so yes.
answers.What does a VOID visit mean? I see 25 of: HIM voids a visit that was registered in error. And since 2018 the ED registrars also VOID the visit when a patient leaves without being seen, because MCS/2 has no other way to close it. Those patients were really there: triage took their vitals. They are not errors and shouldn't vanish from the chart.
answers.What values can RACE_TXT hold?: The picklist text: White, Black or African American, Asian, Hispanic or Latino, American Indian/Alaska Native, Pacific Islander, Other, Declined. Yes, Hispanic is on the race picklist; it should have been an ethnicity question.
answers.When is a problem coded ICD-9 versus ICD: ICD-10 since October 2015, ICD-9 before that. Problems entered without a code are free text the provider typed.
